name: split-flap-text

frames.best_why: The board has settled on 'BERLIN 10:20' with every tile crisp and both captions in place.

tagline: A departure board of dark letter tiles that clacks through to each new phrase.
summary: A split-flap board that scrambles its letter tiles and settles on a new line each cycle, styled like an airport departures sign. Words, timing and tile styling are configurable.
appearance: Rows of small dark rounded tiles each hold one pale monospace capital, split by a faint hinge line across the middle. Sparse uppercase captions sit above and below the board on a black surface.
behaviour: Every character cycles through random glyphs before settling on its target, cascading left to right, then the board holds and moves to the next phrase on a loop.
demo_content: Departure phrases LISBON 09:45, BERLIN 10:20, TOKYO 11:05 and NEW YORK 12:30 under 'Departures, Terminal 2'.
use_when: A headline or status line should feel mechanical and retro, cycling through several short messages.
avoid_when: Every tile runs its own flip loop, which is busy and hard to read for anyone sensitive to motion.
customise: Words or a text string, flip duration, stagger, cycle delay, charset, flips per char, tile and text colours, sizes, alignment and tile style are props.
weight_why: A rAF loop drives up to a dozen tiles through several flips every cycle.

a11y.note: The current phrase is exposed as one text label while the scrambling tiles are hidden from assistive tech.

issues: The tiles spend most of each cycle showing random letters, so a quick screenshot can look like gibberish.
polish_why: Convincing flap shading and a crisp monospace board; the scramble only reads at rest.
title: Split Flap Text
